finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /hooks/test sends a server-side HTTP POST to an arbitrary user-supplied URL. This allows access to internal services and cloud metadata endpoints. The response status is returned, so it also works as a port and host oracle.
finding.source: req.body.callback (JSON or form body of POST /hooks/test)

trace.note: Route handler on the public router `pub`, with no auth middleware
req.body.callback is passed directly to axios.post as the URL
The upstream status code is returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host or allowlist check. No private or link-local IP blocking, and no DNS-rebinding protection. No redirect limits (axios follows redirects by default). The `pub` router is not behind requireAdmin, which is applied only to `admin`. No authentication is visible in this file. I could not see how the router is mounted, since only routes.js is present.

verdict.reason: routes.js:19-21 shows pub.post("/hooks/test") passing req.body.callback straight to axios.post at line 20 and returning r.status at line 21, with no validation and no auth middleware, since requireAdmin is applied only to `admin` at line 12. The mounting is not visible, but nothing in this file restricts the route.

finding.claim: GET /diagnostics/fetch makes a server-side GET request to an arbitrary user-supplied URL. This allows access to internal hosts and cloud metadata. Only the status is returned, but that still gives a blind SSRF and internal port-scan oracle. Exploitation requires an admin session, so severity is lower.

trace.note: req.query.url is passed directly to axios.get

finding.guards_checked: requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10) requires session.role === 'admin', which limits the attacker to admins or to anyone who has compromised or forged an admin session. There is no URL validation, allowlist, private-IP blocking or redirect restriction. Because the admin router could be mounted at a different prefix, I could not confirm it is mounted behind auth.

verdict.guard_found: requireAdmin at routes.js:7-10, applied via admin.use at routes.js:12, returns 403 unless session.role === 'admin'. There is no URL validation.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (routes.js:12, 14, 15), but req.query.url at routes.js:15 is reachable only through the router-level requireAdmin gate (routes.js:7-12), so it is not controllable by an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker. The router's mount point isn't in the code, but the gate is attached to the router itself and applies wherever it is mounted.
